description:
If you’re an athlete, you have to read these books.

All available at the @paintedporchbookshop
transcript: If you're an athlete or you have an athlete in your life, these are the best books about sports and sports psychology that I would recommend. This is Tom Brady's favorite book, The Inner Game of Tennis. Absolutely incredible about the mental side of things. Maybe the greatest lacrosse player of all time. This is The Way of the Champion. Little meditations every day on how to be your best. Chris Bosh, Letters to a Young Athlete. Speaking of tennis, John McPhee's Levels of the Game by Arthur Ashe is absolutely incredible. Love this one. This is one of my favorites, Captain's Class. We think it's all about the star players, the sort of marquee players, the franchise players, but no, it's actually about the team captains, the one that bring all those people together. The team captain is not usually the best player on the team, but they're the most important player on the team in ways that are often hard to measure. Sean Green's The Way of Baseball. I love this book. Recommend this one all the time. This is sort of Zen and baseball, two things that maybe don't go together as often as you think they would. I was lucky enough to work on this book with the great George Ravelyn, who brought Michael Jordan to Nike. It's probably the best basketball book ever written though. Halberstam's The Breaks of the Game. Murakami's What I Talk About When I Talk About Running. Here's another one about writing as a discipline, which I really like, David Epstein's Brain. It's both a parenting book in disguise. It's a business self-help book, but it's also fundamentally about sports. This is just a great book that everyone should read, especially if you're starting to get really good at something or your kids are starting to really get good at something.
